88632.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports).
  2. You are in a quiet test location: nobody else invoices, issues credits or clocks time there this week; on the Dashboard, the Revenue tile on This Week reads $0.00 with 0 Invoices.
  3. You run the whole case on one day, and not on the last evening of the week, so every record you create stays inside This Week.
  4. A test customer with one contact and one asset that uses that contact (for example ZZAUTOTEST Dash Customer 1, contact Dana Test, unit ZZ-101).
  5. Technician 1: a technician at this location, with Time Clock on, whose sign-in you have (you clock time as them in a second browser or a private window).
  6. Advisor A: a name in the work order's Service Advisor list (your own name, Admin ShopView, is filled in by default).
  7. One invoiced work order (not sent, not paid) for that customer, Service Advisor Advisor A, one labor line: What Are You Doing? ZZAUTOTEST Line 1, Technician 1, $100.00 an hour, Estimated Time 2.00, Tech Time 2.00, with exactly 2.00 hours clocked on it. You have written down its Subtotal (e.g. $200.00).

Setup

  • For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on.
  • For 2: to change location, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list; pick ZZAUTOTEST Dashboard Quiet (it already exists and charges 0 % shop supplies). Check: Dashboard > Revenue tile > range pill > This Week: it reads $0.00 with 0 Invoices. If it does not, try another location in the list. Locations cannot be deleted, so do not create another one: if no location is quiet this week, mark the case Blocked and write in the result comment that no quiet location was free this week.
  • For 4: Customers > New Customer > Name > Save; on its Contacts tab: New Contact; add an asset (Add beside Asset in the New Work Order window, or the customer's Assets tab) and pick that contact in the asset's Contact field.
  • For 5: Technician 1: a technician offered in Add Technician at this location whose sign-in you have. If there is none, create one: profile icon > Settings > Staff > New Staff Member: a name (for example ZZAUTOTEST Technician1), an Email you can open, Role Technician, a Department, Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close; accept the invitation email and set a password.
  • For 6: the Service Advisor is in the work order's left panel (it shows your own name by default); to use another advisor, pick another name there.
  • For 7: Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and an Asset (Add beside either if needed) > Save (if a Confirmation says the customer is over their credit limit, click Create); set Service Advisor to Advisor A in the left panel; in the New Line window (> New Line on the Lines tab for each further line): What Are You Doing? ZZAUTOTEST Line 1, Add Technician Technician 1, Labor Rate EVR Travel to EVO ($100 an hour), Estimated Time 2 and Tech Time 2, tick Line Approved > Save & Close; as Technician 1 in a second browser: open the work order > on the line's Labor row click Start, then Stop > Clock Out; as Admin make the clocked time exactly 2.00 hours: three dots at the top right of the Lines tab > Timesheets (1) > edit the record (if it cannot be edited there or in Reports > Timesheet Activities, keep the real time and use the hours Timesheet Activities shows in every sum); on the line click Story (Add tech story for this line) > type a short story > Update; click Complete (if a Missing Details window asks for Mileage, enter one > Complete All Lines); click Mark Reviewed; Finance tab > Create Invoice; close the New Customer Payment window without paying (do not send or pay the invoice). The Subtotal is on the Finance tab.
88632.custom_steps:
1. Click Reports in the top menu, then Sales in the left menu.
  2. Set the Date control to This week.
  3. Write down the row for your invoice and the Subtotal in the Totals row (e.g. $200.00).
  4. Click Advisor Analysis in the left menu (the page is titled Service Advisor Analysis) and set the Date control to This week, with no advisor chosen.
  5. Write down your invoice's row: Hrs Worked, Hrs Invoiced, Billing Efficiency, ELR and Subtotal (e.g. 2.00, 2.00, 100.00%, $200.00).
  6. Click Work Orders in the top menu and open the same work order.
  7. On the Lines tab click New Line: What Are You Doing? "ZZAUTOTEST Line 2", Add Technician = Technician 1, Labor Rate EVR Travel to EVO ($100 an hour), Estimated Time 1.00, Tech Time 1.00, tick Line Approved > Save & Close. (Adding a line while the invoice is still unpaid and unsent voids that invoice.)
  8. On the new line click Story > type a short story > Update, then click Complete (if a window offers Complete All Lines or asks for Mileage, finish it there), then click Mark Reviewed.
  9. Click the Finance tab and write down what it shows for the first invoice (for example a Void label).
  10. Click Create Invoice, close the New Customer Payment dialog without paying, and write down the new Subtotal (e.g. $300.00 = $200.00 + 1.00 hour x $100.00).
  11. Open Reports > Sales again (Date: This week) and write down the rows and the Totals row Subtotal.
  12. Open Reports > Advisor Analysis again (Date: This week, no advisor chosen) and write down the rows and the Totals row.
  13. Try to make an invoice with no customer: Parts > Part Sales > New Part Sale, and see whether the sale can be invoiced without choosing a customer. If the screen insists on a customer, stop this step.
  14. Open the release notes published with this release and look for the note about the Sales and Service Advisor Analysis corrections. The sources do not say where release notes are published: if you cannot find them, write "release note not found" in the result comment and mark only this check Blocked.

88638.custom_steps:
1. Work out the right figure by hand, all hours first: (1.00 + 2.00) / (4.00 + 1.00) x 100 = 3.00 / 5.00 x 100 = 60.00%.
  2. Work out the wrong figure, an average of the two advisors: Advisor A 1.00 / 4.00 = 25.00%, Advisor B 2.00 / 1.00 = 200.00%, average (25.00 + 200.00) / 2 = 112.50%.
  3. Click Dashboard in the top menu.
  4. On the Billing Efficiency tile click the range pill and choose This Week.
  5. Write down the percentage and the line under it.
  6. Click the arrow icon beside "Billing Efficiency" on the tile (its tooltip names the report).
  7. On Service Advisor Analysis set the Date control to This week with no advisor chosen.
  8. Write down each invoice row's Billing Efficiency and the Totals row Billing Efficiency.
88638.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The tile reads 60.00% (3.00 / 5.00 x 100), not 112.50%.
  • The line under it reads "3.00 Invoiced / 5.00 Clocked".
  • The report shows Advisor A's invoice at 25.00% and Advisor B's at 200.00%, and its Totals row reads 60.00%, the same as the tile.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (S3); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, S3 (S3-R2 Billing Efficiency row, S3-R1, context note). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, captured 2026-09-28) used for on-screen labels and navigation only: boards 05_Billing_After, 11_service-advisor-analysis_After.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R2: “Each measure is calculated as defined in the table below.”
  • S3-R2 table row (Billing Efficiency): “| Billing Efficiency | Invoiced hours divided by worked hours, times 100, for the selected range. | Service Advisor Analysis report |”
  • S3-R1: “Every figure the dashboard shows for a measure equals the figure the measure's matching report shows for the same workplace, date range, and filters. This holds at every moment, not merely in principle. The dashboard may serve a figure from a cache, but only in a way that cannot produce a difference: the tile and its report must resolve to the same stored calculation, or the cache must be invalidated by the same events that change the report's answer. A tile that shows a different number from its report because one of them is more recently computed than the other is a defect, not an accepted staleness window. There is no freshness allowance and no "up to N minutes behind" in this spec.”
  • S3 context note (parity check): “to check parity on a KPI tile that shows a shop-wide figure, compare it against the matching report with all advisors or all technicians selected (no filter applied).”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.

88640.custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top menu, set the Technician Efficiency tile's range pill to This Week, and write down what the tile shows.
  2. Create work order 2 for the same customer: Work Orders > Create Work Order > pick the customer and its asset > Save, then set Service Advisor and the mileage.
  3. On the Lines tab click New Line: What Are You Doing? "ZZAUTOTEST Shared", Add Technician = Technician 1, Labor Rate EVR Travel to EVO ($100 an hour), Estimated Time 2.00, Tech Time 2.00, tick Line Approved > Save & Close.
  4. In the second browser, signed in as Technician 1, on that line's Labor row click Start, then Stop > Clock Out. Then sign in as Technician 2 and do the same.
  5. On work order 2 click the three dots > Timesheets (2) and edit the records so Technician 1's runs 2.10 hours (e.g. 8:00 AM to 10:06 AM) and Technician 2's 0.90 hours (e.g. 8:00 AM to 8:54 AM). If they cannot be edited, use the hours shown in Reports > Timesheet Activities in the sums below.
  6. On the line click Story > type a short story > Update, click Complete (finish any Missing Details window), then Mark Reviewed, then Finance > Create Invoice (close the payment dialog without paying).
  7. Work out each share by hand: Technician 1 2.00 x 2.10 / 3.00 = 1.40 hours (70%), Technician 2 2.00 x 0.90 / 3.00 = 0.60 hours (30%). Work order 1's 1.00 hour has no clocked time, so it gives nobody a share.
  8. Work out the tile by hand: (1.40 + 0.60) / (2.10 + 0.90) x 100 = 2.00 / 3.00 x 100 = 66.67%.
  9. Click Dashboard, set Technician Efficiency to This Week and write down the percentage and the line under it.
  10. Click the arrow icon beside "Technician Efficiency" on the tile (its tooltip names the report).
  11. Click the Invoiced tab, make sure the Date control shows This week, and write down Technician 1's and Technician 2's Clocked Hrs, Invoiced Tech Hrs and Efficiency.

  • On the Invoiced tab Technician 1 shows Clocked Hrs 2.10, Invoiced Tech Hrs 1.40, Efficiency 66.67%, and Technician 2 shows 0.90, 0.60 and 66.67%: the line's 2.00 hours are shared 70 / 30 by clocked time.

1. Click Dashboard, set Revenue to This Week and write down the figure ($0.00).
